subject: Is aKDE usable for entire data of a year of a migratory secies

messages.author: 6c64dfc2a1660ab1
messages.subject: Is aKDE usable for entire data of a year of a migratory secies
parts:
Dear Chris,
In the beginning I apologize for my ignorance as question may be to naive to ask here.

I have high resolution (5 min interval)  movement data of vulture which includes wintering homerange, migration and stopover and reaching to breeding homerange.
1. Is it logical to use aKDE for estimation of the stopover sites?
2. Is it even logical to perform aKDE on the entire movement data and separate the wintering, stopover and homerange UDs with help of variogram?

Thanking you,
Dibyendu

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Is aKDE usable for entire data of a year of a migratory secies
parts:
Hi Dibyendu,

It makes sense to run AKDE on the winter ranges and the summer ranges separately.

It makes sense to run AKDE on a stopover site, if they stick around there for a little while, and you have multiple location fixes at that stopover site. And, so it makes sense to run AKDE on multiple stopover sites in the same way.

If you have many migrations, then it makes sense to run AKDE on the stopovers, but unless you have one location per stopover its a little tricky to account for the autocorrelation, and will be slow to converge.
We have better methods in the pipeline for this task, but it's a fundamentally hard statistical problem.

Best,
Chris
